RAMA_NAVAMI.name: Rama Navami
RAMA_NAVAMI.about: Rama Navami, the ninth day of Chaitra's bright half, is the birthday of Rama. Devotees fast and worship him at midday, the hour of his birth, and Janakpur, the city of Sita, draws great crowds.

JANMASHTAMI.name: Krishna Janmashtami
JANMASHTAMI.about: Krishna Janmashtami, the eighth day of Bhadra's dark half, is the birthday of Krishna. Devotees fast until midnight, the hour of his birth, sing bhajans and visit his temples, Patan's Krishna Mandir above all.

VIJAYA_DASHAMI.name: Vijaya Dashami
VIJAYA_DASHAMI.about: Vijaya Dashami, the tenth day, is Dashain's main day, the day of the goddess's victory. From the auspicious hour, the elders put a red tika on the foreheads of the young and jamara behind their ears with a blessing. The visits to relatives for tika go on until the full moon.

LAKSHMI_PUJA.name: Lakshmi Puja
LAKSHMI_PUJA.about: Lakshmi Puja, the new moon of Kartik, is Tihar's main day. In the morning the cow is worshipped as Lakshmi; in the evening the goddess of wealth is welcomed into the house with lamps, a path of red earth from the door to the shrine, and a puja for prosperity in the year ahead. That night the girls' bhailo begins.

HARITALIKA.name: Haritalika Teej
HARITALIKA.about: Haritalika, the third day of Bhadra's bright half, is the day of the Teej fast. Married women fast, many without even water, for their husbands' long life and the family's good, and unmarried women for a good husband, as Parvati did. They worship Shiva and Parvati and spend the day in song and dance.

NAVARATRA_ARAMBHA.name: Navaratra Begins
NAVARATRA_ARAMBHA.about: Ghatasthapana, the first day of Ashwin's bright half, opens Dashain and the nine nights of the Navaratri. A kalash of water is set up as the goddess's seat, and barley and maize are sown beside it in a dark room. Their yellow shoots, the jamara, are given with the tika on Vijaya Dashami.

YAMA_DWITIYA.name: Yama Dwitiya
YAMA_DWITIYA.about: Bhai Tika, the second day of Kartik's bright half, closes Tihar. Sisters pray to Yama for their brothers' long life, give them a tika of seven colours and a garland of makhamali flowers, and feed them; brothers give gifts in return. The day recalls the welcome Yamuna gave her brother Yama.

SHIVARATRI.name: Maha Shivaratri
SHIVARATRI.about: Maha Shivaratri, the fourteenth night of the dark half in Falgun, is the great night of Shiva. Devotees fast and keep vigil through the night, and great crowds, among them sadhus from Nepal and India, come to Pashupatinath. Fires are lit against the last of the winter's cold.

RAKSHABANDHAN.name: Raksha Bandhan
RAKSHABANDHAN.about: Janai Purnima, the full moon of Shrawan, is the day men who wear the sacred thread change it after bathing and the priest's mantras. Everyone receives a protective thread, the doro, on the wrist, and sisters tie rakhi on their brothers' wrists. Pilgrims go to Gosainkunda, and in the valley the Newars eat kwati, a soup of nine beans.

HOLI_HILLS.name: Holi in the Hills
HOLI_HILLS.about: Holi, Fagu Purnima, is the festival of colours at the full moon of Falgun, and the hills keep it a day before the Terai. A week earlier the chir, a pole hung with strips of cloth, is raised at Basantapur in Kathmandu. On the day, people throw coloured powder and water at one another.

HOLI_TERAI.name: Holi in the Terai
HOLI_TERAI.about: The Terai keeps Holi on the day after the hills, as northern India does. The night before, Holika's bonfire recalls the burning of the demoness Holika and the escape of the devotee Prahlad. On the day, people play with colours, visit their neighbours and share sweets.

RISHI_PANCHAMI.name: Rishi Panchami
RISHI_PANCHAMI.about: Rishi Panchami, the fifth day of Bhadra's bright half, closes Teej. Women bathe in rivers, cleansing themselves with twigs of the datiwan plant, and worship the seven sages, the Saptarshi, for purity.

MHA_PUJA.name: Mha Puja
MHA_PUJA.about: Mha Puja, the worship of the body, is kept by the Newars on the first day of Kartik's bright half, which is also the new year of Nepal Sambat. Each member of the family sits before a mandala drawn for them, and the self is worshipped for health and long life in the year ahead.

NEPAL_SAMBAT_NEW_YEAR.name: Nepal Sambat New Year
NEPAL_SAMBAT_NEW_YEAR.about: Nepal Sambat's new year falls on the first day of Kartik's bright half, the day of Mha Puja. The era is held to begin in 879 CE, and the Newars greet it with processions and Mha Puja; the state names Nepal Sambat a national era.

GHODE_JATRA.name: Ghode Jatra
GHODE_JATRA.about: Ghode Jatra, the horse festival, falls on the new moon of Chaitra. The Nepal Army holds horse races and displays at Tundikhel, said to keep down the demon Tundi buried beneath it, and the valley's goddesses are carried in procession.

SANKASHTA_CHATURTHI.name: Sankashta Chaturthi
SANKASHTA_CHATURTHI.prose: Sankashta chaturthi, the dark fourth at moonrise

MESHA_SANKRANTI.name: Mesha Sankranti
MESHA_SANKRANTI.prose: Mesha sankranti, the Bikram Sambat new year
MESHA_SANKRANTI.about: Mesha Sankranti, the first of Baishakh, is the new year of Bikram Sambat, Nepal's official calendar, the day the Sun enters Aries. People greet the new year, and in Bhaktapur the Bisket Jatra pulls Bhairav's chariot and raises the yosin pole.

KARKATA_SANKRANTI.name: Karkata Sankranti
KARKATA_SANKRANTI.prose: Karkata sankranti, the sun's turn south

MAKARA_SANKRANTI.name: Makara Sankranti
MAKARA_SANKRANTI.prose: Makara sankranti, the sun's turn north
MAKARA_SANKRANTI.about: Maghe Sankranti, the first of Magh, is the day the Sun enters Capricorn and turns north, toward the warmer half of the year. Families eat sesame laddus, chaku, ghee, sweet potato and yam, and bathe at holy confluences such as Devghat. The Tharu keep the day as Maghi, their new year.

UTTARAYANA_ARAMBHA.name: Uttarayana Arambha
UTTARAYANA_ARAMBHA.prose: Uttarayana arambha, the sun's turn north

DAKSHINAYANA_ARAMBHA.name: Dakshinayana Arambha
DAKSHINAYANA_ARAMBHA.prose: Dakshinayana arambha, the sun's turn south

RASHTRIYA_EKATA_DIWAS.prose: Rashtriya Ekata Diwas, National Unity Day

GHYA_CHAKU_SALHU.name: Ghya Chaku Salhu
GHYA_CHAKU_SALHU.prose: Ghya Chaku Salhu, Maghe Sankranti in Nepal Bhasa

SHATABIJ_ROPAN.name: Shatabij Ropan
SHATABIJ_ROPAN.prose: Shatabij Ropan, the sowing of a hundred seeds

NIMKO_PAAT_KHANE_DIN.name: Nimko Paat Khane Din
NIMKO_PAAT_KHANE_DIN.prose: Nimko Paat Khane Din, the day neem leaves are eaten

MOHARATRI.name: Moharatri
MOHARATRI.prose: Moharatri, the night of Krishna's birth

NAYA_BARSHA.name: Naya Barsha
NAYA_BARSHA.prose: Naya Barsha, the Bikram Sambat new year

NEPAL_SAMBAT_ARAMBHA.name: Nepal Sambat Arambha
NEPAL_SAMBAT_ARAMBHA.prose: Nepal Sambat Arambha, the beginning of the Nepal Sambat year

SONAM_LHOSAR.name: Sonam Lhosar
SONAM_LHOSAR.prose: Sonam Lhosar, the Tamang new year
SONAM_LHOSAR.about: Sonam Lhosar, the new moon of Magh, is the new year of the Tamang people. Families clean their homes and visit the monastery, and the new year is greeted with songs and dances to the damphu drum.

TAMU_LHOSAR.name: Tamu Lhosar
TAMU_LHOSAR.prose: Tamu Lhosar, the Gurung new year, Poush 15
TAMU_LHOSAR.about: Tamu Lhosar, on the fifteenth of Poush, is the new year of the Gurung people, the turn of their twelve-year cycle. Gurungs gather in traditional dress and greet the year with feasts, songs and dances.

GYALPO_LHOSAR.name: Gyalpo Lhosar
GYALPO_LHOSAR.prose: Gyalpo Lhosar, the Sherpa and Tibetan new year
GYALPO_LHOSAR.about: Gyalpo Lhosar, the new moon of Falgun, is the new year of the Sherpa and other Himalayan Buddhist peoples, the first day of the Tibetan calendar. Monasteries hold prayers and masked dances, prayer flags are renewed, and families visit one another.

RATO_MACHHINDRANATH_RATH_JATRA_BEGINS.name: Rato Machhindranath Rath Jatra Begins
RATO_MACHHINDRANATH_RATH_JATRA_BEGINS.about: Rato Machhindranath's chariot festival, the longest in Patan, begins when the god of rain is set on his towering chariot. Over the following weeks the chariot is pulled through Patan to Jawalakhel. There, at Bhoto Jatra, the god's jewelled vest, the bhoto, is held up for all to see.

BUDDHA_JAYANTI.name: Buddha Jayanti
BUDDHA_JAYANTI.about: Buddha Jayanti, the full moon of Baishakh, marks the birth of the Buddha at Lumbini in Nepal, and also his enlightenment and his passing. Buddhists visit Lumbini and the stupas of Swayambhu and Boudha, light lamps and give alms.

UBHAULI.name: Ubhauli
UBHAULI.about: Ubhauli, the full moon of Baishakh, is the Kirat peoples' festival of spring, when the Rai, Limbu, Yakkha and Sunuwar begin the year's farming and move up toward the hills. They worship nature and their ancestors for good crops, and dance the sakela in great circles.

GAI_JATRA.name: Gai Jatra
GAI_JATRA.about: Gai Jatra, the day after Janai Purnima, is the Newar procession for those who died in the year. Each bereaved family sends a cow, or a child dressed as one, around the city. The day has also become one of satire and comedy.

INDRA_JATRA.name: Indra Jatra
INDRA_JATRA.about: Indra Jatra is Kathmandu's great festival of Bhadra, honouring Indra, the god of rain. A tall pole, the lingo, is raised at Hanuman Dhoka, masked dancers fill the squares, and the living goddess Kumari is pulled through the old city in her chariot.

JITIYA.name: Jitiya
JITIYA.about: Jitiya, the Jivitputrika vrata of Ashwin's dark half, is kept by the mothers of Mithila and of the Tharu people. They fast, without even water, for their children's long life and well-being.

PHULPATI.name: Phulpati
PHULPATI.about: Phulpati, the seventh day of Dashain, brings the goddess in as a bundle of sacred leaves, flowers and fruit. The royal phulpati is carried from Gorkha and received in Kathmandu with a procession and an army salute on its way to Hanuman Dhoka. Each home brings its own into the room where the jamara grows.

MAHA_ASHTAMI.name: Maha Ashtami
MAHA_ASHTAMI.about: Maha Ashtami, the eighth day of Dashain, is given to the fiercest forms of the goddess, Kali and the valley's Taleju. Offerings are made at her temples through the day and through the night that follows, the Kalaratri.

KUKUR_TIHAR.name: Kukur Tihar
KUKUR_TIHAR.about: Kukur Tihar, the second day of Tihar, honours the dog as the messenger of Yama, the god of death. Dogs are given a tika and a garland of flowers and fed well.

GOVARDHAN_PUJA.name: Govardhan Puja
GOVARDHAN_PUJA.about: Govardhan Puja, the first day of Kartik's bright half, recalls Krishna lifting Mount Govardhan to shelter the people of Braj from Indra's storm. A small hill of cow dung is made and worshipped as the mountain, and oxen are honoured with tika and garlands.

CHHATH.name: Chhath
CHHATH.about: Chhath is the Terai's and Mithila's festival of the Sun and of Chhathi Maiya, kept over four days of Kartik's bright half. Worshippers fast, without water from Kharna, and stand in rivers and ponds to offer arghya to the setting Sun on the sixth and to the rising Sun the next morning. The offerings of thekua, fruit and sugarcane are carried in bamboo baskets.

GURU_NANAK_JAYANTI.name: Guru Nanak Jayanti
GURU_NANAK_JAYANTI.about: Guru Nanak Jayanti, the full moon of Kartik, is the birthday of Guru Nanak, the first Guru of the Sikhs. Sikhs read the Guru Granth Sahib through, take out processions, and serve a free meal to all at the gurdwara's langar.

UDHAULI.name: Udhauli
UDHAULI.about: Udhauli, the full moon of Mangsir, is the Kirat peoples' festival of the harvest and of the move down toward the warmer valleys before winter. They thank nature and their ancestors for the crops and dance the sakela again.

BASANTA_PANCHAMI.name: Basanta Panchami
BASANTA_PANCHAMI.about: Basanta Panchami, the fifth day of Magh's bright half, welcomes spring and honours Saraswati, the goddess of learning. Students worship her at schools and temples, and small children are taught their first letters.

MAGHI_THARU.name: Maghi
MAGHI_THARU.prose: Maghi, the Tharu new year, Magh 1
MAGHI_THARU.about: Maghi, the first of Magh, is the new year of the Tharu people and their greatest festival. Families feast, villages choose their headman, the badghar, for the year, and the days are spent in dances and visits.

CHRISTMAS.name: Christmas
CHRISTMAS.about: Christmas, on 25 December, celebrates the birth of Jesus Christ. Christians go to church services, sing carols, decorate their homes, and share meals and gifts.

GAURA_PARVA.name: Gaura Parva
GAURA_PARVA.about: Gaura is the great festival of Nepal's far west, kept in Bhadra for the goddess Gaura, Parvati, and for Shiva. Women fast and soak five grains, the biruda, and the villages dance the deuda through the nights.

EID_AL_FITR.name: Eid al-Fitr
EID_AL_FITR.about: Eid al-Fitr ends Ramadan, the month of fasting, on the first day of Shawwal, once the new crescent is seen. Muslims gather for the Eid prayer, give zakat al-fitr to the poor, and visit and feast with family and friends.

EID_AL_ADHA.name: Eid al-Adha
EID_AL_ADHA.about: Eid al-Adha, the feast of the sacrifice on the tenth of Dhu al-Hijja, recalls Ibrahim's readiness to sacrifice his son at God's command. After the Eid prayer, families who can sacrifice an animal and share its meat with relatives and the poor.

TEEJ.name: Teej
TEEJ.about: Teej is the women's festival of Bhadra's bright half, kept for Parvati, who fasted to win Shiva as her husband. It runs from the feast of the dar, through the fast of Haritalika, to the bath of Rishi Panchami. Women dress in red, and sing and dance at Shiva's temples.

DASHAIN.name: Dashain
DASHAIN.about: Dashain is Nepal's longest and most widely kept festival, fifteen days of the bright half of Ashwin. It honours the goddess Durga and recalls her victory over the demon Mahishasura, the triumph of good over evil. Families gather from far away, and the elders give the young tika and jamara with their blessing.

TIHAR.name: Tihar
TIHAR.about: Tihar, the festival of lights, is kept over five days as Kartik's dark half turns into its bright half. Its days honour in turn the crow, the dog, the cow and Lakshmi, the goddess of wealth, and the ox and the self, and they end with Bhai Tika, when sisters honour their brothers. Houses are cleaned and lit with lamps, and groups go from house to house singing deusi and bhailo.
